title: Sheaves on an essentially small site have a flat separator (Lean split)
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$, and let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category with a symmetric monoidal closed structure whose tensor product is additive in each variable. Call an object $P$ of $\mathcal A$ (resp. of the category $\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C,J;\mathcal A)$ of $\mathcal A$-valued sheaves, with the monoidal structure obtained by sheafifying the objectwise tensor product) *flat* if tensoring with $P$ preserves finite limits, and a *separator* if for every two distinct parallel morphisms $u\neq v:M\to N$ there is a morphism $h:P\to M$ with $u h\neq v h$. If $\mathcal A$ has an object that is both flat and a separator, then so does $\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C,J;\mathcal A)$. (For $\mathcal A$ the category of $\Lambda$-modules and $\mathcal C$ the small étale site of a scheme, such an object is $\bigoplus_U j_{U!}\Lambda_U$, the sum over the objects $U$ of extension by zero of the constant sheaf.)

proof.text: Step 1 (the sheaf category and the meaning of flat). By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed], $\mathcal S:=\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C,J;\mathcal A)$ is a Grothendieck abelian category, and with the sheafified objectwise tensor product it is symmetric monoidal closed. Hence for a sheaf $Q$ the functors $Q\otimes-$ and $-\otimes Q$ are left adjoints, so they preserve all colimits, in particular finite colimits; and the symmetry gives $Q\otimes-\cong-\otimes Q$. So $Q$ is flat in the sense of the statement (tensoring with $Q$ preserves finite limits) if and only if both $Q\otimes-$ and $-\otimes Q$ are exact (preserve finite limits and finite colimits), which is the notion of flat object of the Lean declaration (`ObjectProperty.flat`; the equivalence is `ObjectProperty.flat_iff_preservesFiniteLimits`). The same holds in $\mathcal A$, which is symmetric monoidal closed by hypothesis.

source.place: agent: generalization of Lemma 0GMW (sheafified tensor product) and Lemma 03EO (tensor-Hom adjunction) to A-valued sheaves; Lean module docstring of WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckAbelian.Monoidal.FlatResolution (slopmaster2), section "The sheaf case"

proof.text: Step 2 (the candidate and the separator half). Let $G$ be an object of $\mathcal A$ that is flat and a separator. For each object $X$ of $\mathcal C$ let $G_X^\#$ be the sheaf associated to the presheaf $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{\varphi\in\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(V,X)}G$, i.e. $j_{X!}\underline G_X$, the extension by zero of the constant sheaf $G$ on $\mathcal C/X$ (Stacks 03DI); it represents $F\mapsto\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(G,F(X))$. Since $\mathcal S$ is Grothendieck abelian (Step 1) it has all coproducts indexed by sets of the size of its Hom-sets; the objects of $\mathcal C$ form such a set (in the Lean statement $\mathcal C:\mathrm{Type}(u+1)$ and the Hom-sets of $\mathcal S$ live in $\mathrm{Type}(u+1)$; alternatively, since $\mathcal C$ is essentially small one may sum only over a set of representatives of the isomorphism classes of objects, $G_X^\#\cong G_{X'}^\#$ for $X\cong X'$). Put $S:=\coprod_{X\in\mathrm{Ob}(\mathcal C)}G_X^\#$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-free-separator] (the sheaves $G_X^\#$ detect morphisms because $\mathrm{Hom}(G_X^\#,F)=\mathrm{Hom}(G,F(X))$, $G$ separates in $\mathcal A$ and a morphism of sheaves is determined by its components), $S$ is a separator of $\mathcal S$.

proof.text: Step 3 (each summand is flat). $G$ is flat in $\mathcal A$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-free-sheaf-flat] applied with $P=G$, each $G_X^\#=j_{X!}\underline G_X$ is flat in $\mathcal S$: $G_X^\#\otimes-$ preserves finite limits. (For $\mathcal A$ the category of $\mathcal O$-modules this is Stacks 03EV (2).)

source.place: Lemma 03EV (lemma-j-shriek-flat), generalized to A-valued sheaves in [lem-weil-pbc-free-sheaf-flat]

proof.text: Step 4 (the sum is flat). $\mathcal S$ is Grothendieck abelian with a braided (indeed symmetric) monoidal closed structure (Step 1), and $(G_X^\#)_{X\in\mathrm{Ob}(\mathcal C)}$ is a family of flat objects indexed by a set of the size of the Hom-sets of $\mathcal S$ (Steps 2, 3). By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-coproduct] applied to $\mathcal B=\mathcal S$, $S=\coprod_XG_X^\#$ is flat.

Step 5 (conclusion and the étale case). By Steps 2 and 4, $S$ is an object of $\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C,J;\mathcal A)$ that is a separator and flat; by Step 1 it is flat in the two-sided exact sense as well. For $\mathcal A$ the category of $\Lambda$-modules, $G=\Lambda$ is a flat separator ($\mathrm{Hom}(\Lambda,M)=M$, $\Lambda\otimes_\Lambda-=\mathrm{id}$), and for $\mathcal C$ the small étale site of a scheme, $S=\bigoplus_Uj_{U!}\Lambda_U$, the sum over the objects $U$.
